`echo`: display a line of text.

## Synopsis

<strong>echo</strong> \[<strong>-n</strong>\] \[<em>word</em>...\]

## Description

<strong>echo</strong> writes its <em>word</em>s to standard output, separated by single spaces, followed by a new line.

## Options

<strong>-n</strong>
: Do not write the trailing new line. Only a first argument of <strong>-n</strong> is taken as the option; anywhere else it is a word.

## Exit status

Always 0.

## Examples

```text
echo hello world
echo -n "no new line"
echo $PATH
```

## Notes

<strong>echo</strong> is a program, not a shell builtin. It does not interpret backslash escapes, and has no <strong>-e</strong> or <strong>-E</strong>.

## See also

<strong>sh</strong>(1), <strong>cat</strong>(1)
